page: Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-2560s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute virtual machine provisioned on dedicated AMD EPYC hardware. Configured with an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supporting simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is substantial at 128.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per thread. The configuration includes 2560 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address, without integrated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark measurements indicate exceptional memory performance alongside reliable compute capacity. In large-block memory transfers, the instance achieves top-tier results with uncached write speeds reaching 170.21 GB/sec and uncached read throughput measuring 339.94 GB/sec. Standard compute benchmarks align with the middle tier, yielding a Geekbench 6 multi-core score of 12675.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 37081.08. Stress-ng single-core performance registers in the upper quartile at 2927.78, supported by instruction sets including AVX, AES, and SHA-NI.

The balance between dense RAM allocation and high-capacity NVMe storage provides strong resource efficiency for memory-bound workloads. While raw multi-core compute throughput remains mid-range due to the 2.0 GHz clock speed, the bundled 2.5 TB NVMe disk eliminates reliance on separate network storage for data-heavy tasks. This configuration is well matched for in-memory databases, large Redis deployments, analytical data processing, caching tiers, and enterprise database systems requiring low-latency storage access.

It provides 16 vCPUs over 8 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of RAM and 2560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking GPU acceleration, the platform directs its resources toward memory-heavy and disk-intensive execution. Benchmark evaluations show top-decile large-block memory write throughput of 170.21 GB/sec and strong uncached read speeds of 339.94 GB/sec, while general CPU benchmarks such as Geekbench multi-core (12675.0) and PassMark CPU (37081.08) demonstrate stable mid-tier compute capabilities. This server type is structured for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory databases, caching services, ETL pipelines, and high-capacity transactional data stores.
